handoff.purpose: Define egress gate, gh failure classification, bus transcript reconstruction, publish_to_pr, and read_pr_thread functions.

symbols.name: screen_egress
symbols.note: Scans channels and paths for secrets using secret_floor_rule; returns first hit or None.

symbols.name: _gh_argv
symbols.note: Builds gh command line with optional --repo flag.

symbols.name: _classify_failure
symbols.note: Maps gh invocation failure to (status, detail) tuple.

symbols.name: _first_url
symbols.note: Extracts first http/https URL from text.

symbols.name: load_for_publish
symbols.note: Reconstructs verdict and turns from stored bus transcript.

symbols.name: publish_to_pr
symbols.note: Renders markdown, runs egress gate, optionally invokes gh to post PR comment.

symbols.name: read_pr_thread
symbols.note: Reads PR comments via gh and returns structured turns.

symbols.name: _parse_comment
symbols.note: Converts gh comment JSON to PRTurn.

claims.text: Returns ``(channel, rule)`` for the FIRST hit, or None if clean.
claims.why: Code returns immediately on first hit and returns None after loops.

claims.text: The returned rule is a fixed label / path fragment from ``sensitivity`` -- never matched text, so a refusal can be logged and reported without re-leaking the secret it refused
claims.why: secret_floor_rule is not defined in this chunk; its return value cannot be verified.

claims.text: Auth is tested before not-found because GitHub answers 404 -- not 403 -- for a private repo you are not authenticated to see; classifying that as ``pr_not_found`` would send an operator hunting for a PR that exists and is merely invisible to a logged-out CLI.
claims.why: Code checks auth patterns before not-found patterns in the if-elif chain.

claims.text: ``(verdict, turns)`` reconstructed from a stored bus transcript.

The council package stores no ``outcome`` and no ``convergence`` field -- by construction, because it promotes nothing -- so none is invented here, and :func:`render_markdown` prints "(not recorded)" for them.
claims.why: render_markdown is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify what it prints.

claims.text: Quorum comes from the roster records' ``participants``: a vendor is ANSWERED only if it actually produced a turn, not if it was merely seated.
claims.why: Code adds vendor to answered only if record type 'turn' and status 'spoke'.

claims.text: ``dry_run=True`` renders and gates but does NOT invoke the runner at all; the markdown comes back on the result. The gate still runs, so a dry run is an honest rehearsal rather than a way around the floor.
claims.why: Code runs screen_egress before checking dry_run, and returns early with markdown without invoking runner.

claims.text: The body goes to gh on STDIN via ``--body-file -``: a deliberation exceeds the Windows argv limit, and stdin keeps the payload inspectable by a fake runner in tests exactly as argv would be.
claims.why: Code constructs argv with '--body-file', '-' and passes body via run(argv, body) as second argument.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure -- every outcome is a status in ``PUBLISH_STATUSES``.
claims.why: PUBLISH_STATUSES not defined in this chunk; cannot verify all statuses are in it.

claims.text: Nothing read here is authoritative: a reply is INPUT to a later round, not a verdict, and it is not on the hash-chained bus until the council appends it there.
claims.why: Function returns turns from gh comments; no claim to authority.

observations.what: screen_egress scans channels dict and paths list for secrets using secret_floor_rule.
_classify_failure checks for gh missing, auth failure, rate limit, PR not found, and generic error in that order.
load_for_publish reconstructs verdict dict and turns list from bus transcript, with detailed docstring explaining the logic.
publish_to_pr runs egress gate before any gh invocation; returns early if secret detected or dry_run.
read_pr_thread runs egress gate on pr reference and repo slug before invoking gh.
_parse_comment is partially defined; handles author shapes but truncated.
